subject: Sizing guidance and reserve strategy for Dedicated capacity (long-context + embeddings)
messages:
From: Emma Taylor <emma.taylor@clearwave.ai>

Cc: procurement@clearwave.ai
Date: 2028-11-14T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Request: Dedicated sizing rec for long-context + embeddings workload

Hi Rishi,

We're kicking off sizing for ClearWave's planned Dedicated deployment with Redwood and wanted your engineering insight before we lock commits. High-level workload notes:
- Two main routes: 'Research Chat' (avg. 15 QPS, burst to 120 QPS, typical context 30k-60k tokens, heavy KV/cache usage) and 'Vector Lookup' (embeddings generation + nearest-neighbor, spikes to 400 qps in ingest windows).
- Latency target: 95th < 300ms for chat (interactive); bulk embeddings can tolerate higher latency but we need throughput.
- Long-term expected growth 2.3x over 12 months.

Questions:
1) Given this mix, what's your recommended SKU split between H100 / A100 / L4 for Reserved Dedicated? We care about memory headroom for KV cache for chat and cost per token for embeddings.
2) How much reserve headroom do you recommend (slot counts) for burst safety and failover?
3) Any suggested fallback policy (e.g., degrade to L4 for non-long-context requests) and operational impacts?

I've attached our SOC/DPA questions and a sample traffic histogram. Can you sketch a proposal we can review with procurement?

Thanks,
Emma Taylor
Senior Cloud Architect
ClearWave Labs

Hi Emma —

Thanks for the traffic sketch, this is the exact kind of detail we need. I did a quick pass and attached a short options brief (redwood_fleet_sku_options_v1.pdf) showing three feasible lanes:

- Memory-first (H100-heavy): H100s for the primary chat pool (long contexts + KV cache), A100s for mixed inference, L4s only for small-batch burst/low-cost endpoints. Pros: minimal cache evictions, best 95p latency. Cons: cost premium for reserved H100s.
- Balanced (A100-centric): A100 reserve for most traffic, with an H100 headroom pool for the largest contexts and an L4 pool for cost-sensitive background embeddings. Pros: lower committed spend, workable cache with tiling. Cons: more cache management work and slightly higher 95p latency for the biggest chats.
- Cost-first (L4 + A100 tiling): L4s for most embeddings and short-context chat, A100 tiling for occasional long-context. Pros: cheapest; Cons: complex fallback logic and potential quality/latency degradation.

If you're ok, I'd like to loop Dev to sketch the slot math and an ops-safe fallback policy. Also copying Laura to start sketching commit tiers and commercial impact.

Can we do a 45-min deep-dive Tuesday?

—Rishi

Rishi / Laura —

Following up with a technical sketch. I'll keep the math explicit so procurement can see the tradeoffs. Quick assumptions:
- Model: we assume a 70B long-context variant with ~60k KV cache growth for the Research Chat path.
- H100 (80GB), A100 (40GB), L4 (24GB) effective usable memory for KV after model memory: estimate per-slot KV headroom: H100 ~36–40GB, A100 ~10–14GB (tiling helps), L4 ~2–6GB.

Slot sizing:
- Chat pool (latency-sensitive): for stable 15 QPS baseline with spikes to 120 QPS (p99 allocation), we recommend reserving 12 H100 slots to maintain avg 95p latency target with KV pinning. Rationale: each H100 slot (pinned) can sustain several simultaneous long-context sessions when KV cached — but safe headroom required to avoid costly cache thrash.
- Mixed inference (embeddings + short chat): use 18 A100 slots sized for balanced throughput; these handle medium contexts and most embeddings at better cost than H100. We rely on batching for embeddings windows.
- Burst/cheap pool: 24 L4 instances for queued, non-urgent embeddings and short-context chat fallback. Use asynchronous worker lanes for large bulk jobs.

Fallback & routing policy:
- Policy: Route 100% of Research Chat to H100 by default. When H100 utilization > 85% for 30s, overflow to A100 if request context <= 12k tokens; overflow to L4 only for non-interactive requests (batch embeddings, background jobs). Explicitly block L4 for >8k contexts to avoid quality loss.
- KV cache strategy: keep a pinned prefix cache on H100s for active research sessions; time-based eviction 30m after inactivity. Provide sticky routing by session id to maintain cache affinity.

Cost impact (ballpark, monthly reserved):
- 12 H100 reserved slots: material premium vs A100 (30–40% uplift) but reduces per-token latency SLO misses for Research Chat.
- A100 pool reduces commit cost while still allowing controlled fallback. L4s drive down unit cost for bulk embeddings by ~3–4x versus H100.

Operational notes:
- We will need a canary rollout for fallback rules (gradual traffic shifting to L4 to observe quality regressions).
- Observability: token-level latency and prompt-set regressions tied to test prompts (we'll include per-route evals).
- Edge case: sustained long bursts (>10 min) will need short-term burst credits (we can propose a burst capacity add-on).

I'll prepare numeric throughput estimates for the call — want me to assume 2.3x 12-month growth now or leave growth out of the first pass?

—Dev Patel
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
